subject: DPA: backup retention & lawful access carveout — Acme negotiation
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmepharm.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: acme-contracts@acmepharm.com
Date: 2027-09-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: DPA redlines: retention, backups and lawful access

Marcus —

Thanks for sending the initial DPA. Attached are our redlines (DPA_redlines_Acme.docx). A couple of high-level asks from Acme Legal that we need to resolve before we can proceed to procurement: 

- Erasure window: we require confirmation that customer data (including derivatives) is removed from all live systems within 7 calendar days of a valid deletion request.
- Backups: we do not accept multi-month backup retention. Our preference is max 30 days for any recoverable snapshot.
- Lawful access carveout: if Redwood receives a law enforcement request, Acme requires notice and a narrow scope limitation; requests should be supported by a warrant and Redwood should object to overbroad requests where permissible.
- Certification: Acme needs a process and a certificate of erasure/attestation that covers active and backup deletion.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can meet these and provide a suggested counter-language? Also attach any SOC 2/ISO evidence or a link to the compliance pack.

Appreciate a turn-around by EOD tomorrow if possible — procurement is on a tight timeline.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Senior Counsel, Acme Pharmaceuticals

Attachment: DPA_redlines_Acme.docx (document with inline comments)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmepharm.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-01T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA redlines: retention, backups and lawful access

Samantha —

Thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. Looping in Neha (Legal) and Vanessa (Prod Ops) to make sure we capture operational constraints. Quick summary of where Redwood stands and the proposal we can take to your team: 

1) Active data deletion: we can commit to removing customer-identifiable active data from serving and active storage within 7 calendar days of a verified deletion instruction. We will provide an attestation once that process completes.

2) Backups/snapshots: operational backups are created on a regular snapshot cycle. Our ops baseline is that backups may remain recoverable for up to 45 days due to snapshot chaining and restore safety. To get closer to your 30-day requirement we can:
   - Offer a contractual maximum of 30 days for recoverable production snapshots for EU-data-scoped customers where feasible, coupled with an internal runbook to prioritize Agreed Customer Erasures during the snapshot retention window.
   - For archival/long-term backups (rare, e.g., for regulatory holds), we propose a separate opt-in archival agreement with explicit retention terms.

3) Lawful access: Redwood will notify the customer of any legal process that requests customer data unless prohibited by law. We will limit disclosures to the narrow scope of the legal demand where possible and will challenge requests that are overbroad. We need to confirm whether Acme requires prior notice language that includes a carveout for emergency or national security orders (these often prohibit notice).

4) Certification: we can provide a deletion attestation for active data within 7 days. For backups, we can provide a certification that we have taken all commercially reasonable steps to remove the data from recoverable backup snapshots within the agreed retention period; for snapshots already in-progress at the time of request we may need up to one snapshot cycle to fully surface deletions (we propose documenting that as part of the DPA).

I attached a short excerpt with proposed redline language (Redwood_proposed_DPA_excerpt.pdf). If Acme can accept a 30-day contractual maximum for recoverable snapshots, plus an archival opt-in and the lawful access language above, we think we can close this quickly.

Would you be open to a 30-minute call tomorrow to resolve the final sentence-level items?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: Redwood_proposed_DPA_excerpt.pdf

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick reply and the excerpt. A few clarifications from our side: 

- 30 days for recoverable snapshots is closer to acceptable, but Acme will need absolute contractual maximum of 30 days (no 45-day operational baseline exceptions).
- On lawful access: we can accept the standard carveout for national security or similar orders, but Acme expects Redwood to push back on requests directed at broad classes of customer data and to provide a log of all production accesses tied to legal demands.
- Certification: Acme requires a fairly specific attestation template certifying both active deletion and the non-recoverability of the data from backups after the 30-day window. Please point us to a sample attestation or confirm you can sign our attestation template (attached; Acme_commented.pdf).

Also, please share SOC 2 Type II report or the compliance summary link you referenced.

Samantha

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-02T10:20:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA redlines: retention, backups and lawful access

Marcus / Vanessa —

I reviewed Samantha's comments and Marcus's proposed excerpt. Operationally there are a few levers we can offer as contractual guardrails to meet Acme's 30-day ask without breaking restore safety: 

- Contractual language: set 30 days as the contractual maximum for recoverable production snapshots for EU-scoped customers. Add language that Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to accelerate snapshot expungement for deletion requests received mid-cycle and will avoid creating new snapshots containing the deleted data after the request.

- Archival carveout: keep archival copies strictly opt-in and documented in a separate SOW/addendum. Default behavior is no long-term archival beyond the 30-day snapshot window.

- Lawful access: propose narrow clause that requires Redwood to (a) notify customer of requests unless prohibited, (b) limit disclosures to the scope of the demand, and (c) provide a report of production accesses tied to legal demands. Add a confidentiality-preserving mechanism for notice if an order prohibits disclosure (e.g., sealed notification to counsel).

- Certification: agree to provide an attestation within 21 calendar days after the deletion attestation for active data; for backups we can provide an attestation that describes the steps taken and the dates by which data will no longer be recoverable (i.e., within the 30-day contractual window). We should review Acme's template and mark any redlines.

Operational note for Vanessa: please confirm whether we need a special runbook change to prioritize deletion requests for customers who have the 30-day contractual mandate. Also confirm whether snapshot chaining means any edge cases where data could persist beyond 30 days in rare failure modes and whether we can mitigate those.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Bcc: acme-contracts@acmepharm.com
Date: 2027-09-03T09:15:00Z
Subject: Final DPA compromise proposal & next steps

Samantha —

Thanks for the candid notes and for running this on Acme's side. Based on Neha and Vanessa's input, here's a proposed compromise for your redline review: 

- Active data: deletion from active systems within 7 calendar days of a verified deletion request; attestation provided within 7 days of completion.
- Recoverable snapshots: contractual maximum retention of 30 days for recoverable production snapshots for EU-scoped customer data; Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to remove data from in-flight snapshots and will not create new snapshots containing deleted data after the request.
- Archival: long-term archival is opt-in only and must be executed via a separate SOW/addendum (default = no archival beyond 30 days).
- Lawful access: Redwood will notify customer of legal demands unless prohibited, limit disclosure to the narrow scope of the demand, and maintain an auditable log of disclosures tied to legal requests. Where notice is prohibited, Redwood will, where allowed, provide a confidential notification to customer's counsel.
- Certification: Redwood will provide an active deletion attestation within 7 days and a backup-removal attestation describing dates and steps taken within 21 days.

I've attached a one-page mutual action plan and language snippets (MutualActionPlan_Acme_20270903.pdf). If Acme accepts the 30-day snapshot maximum plus the opt-in archival model, we can mark the DPA closed and move to DocuSign.

Would you be available for a 30-minute alignment call today at 3pm UTC to finalize the few sentence-level items? If so, I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
